answer: Agents must lock stake before influencing a shared reputation ledger, and proven fraud lets others slash it. Influence depends on stake and verified history, not account count, so splitting funds among fake identities creates no extra power. A newcomer can earn trust through useful work, but an attacker risks real capital and pays fees for each account. Coordinated fraud can expose linked identities, whether agents manage a bridge, map a dune, or tend an orchard.
